item.title: Bash Techniques for Checking if an Array Contains a Specific Value
item.description:
“Bash Techniques for Checking if an Array Contains a Specific Value”

How do you efficiently verify if a specific element (a “needle”) is present within a Bash array (the “haystack”)? Various techniques exist, each with trade-offs concerning performance, handling of special characters (like spaces, null bytes, or newlines), and reliance on external utilities or Bash features. Below, we examine several accepted solutions for this common scripting requirement.

Solution 1: Using Bash Regex Matching (=~) on a String Expansion

This method leverages the power of Bash’s built-in regular expression operator (=~). It implicitly joins array elements into a single string using the first character of IFS (Internal Field Separator) when using ${array[*]}.

item.title: Shell Scripting: Multiple Methods to Extract Substring by Delimiter or Position
item.description:
“Shell Scripting: Multiple Methods to Extract Substring by Delimiter or Position”

When processing filenames or complex strings in a shell environment, extracting a specific segment—such as a numeric ID situated between two underscores—is a frequent requirement. How can one efficiently achieve this substring extraction using various shell tools and built-in features, ensuring high performance and adaptability?

This discussion details numerous accepted solutions for isolating parts of a string, ranging from zero-cost native shell operations to powerful external utilities like cut, sed, and grep.
